official.deadline_note: Postgraduate applications for the 2027 intake close 31 October 2026; undergraduate applications closed 30 September 2026. UCT advises applicants to check the relevant faculty for programme-specific requirements and deadlines, which may close earlier.
official.status_note: UCT states applications are open for the 2027 intake; undergraduate applications are now closed while postgraduate applications (honours, postgraduate diploma, coursework master's) remain open until 31 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Comprehensive financial support covering tuition fees for your chosen programme of study, a laptop, accommodation on UCT's campuses, living expenses, medical aid, a study visa (where applicable) and annual travel to and from UCT.
benefits: Comprehensive financial support covering tuition fees for the chosen programme of study, a laptop, accommodation on UCT's campuses, living expenses, medical aid, a study visa (where applicable) and annual travel to and from UCT
Access to excellent teaching and a transformative and socially engaged education
Academic and peer support to ensure academic development, growth and success
Skills programmes developing entrepreneurial and career readiness skills, capabilities as an ethical and transformative leader, and the ability to keep contributing to the community
Membership of the lifelong Mastercard Foundation Scholars Alumni Network of changemakers
Access to an internship opportunity and costs related to community activities as prescribed by the programme
eligibility: Be a citizen of an African country, including South Africa

Be applying for a first bachelor's degree, or an eligible taught postgraduate programme at UCT: a postgraduate diploma offered by the Faculty of Health Sciences, an honours degree offered by any of UCT's six faculties, or a coursework master's programme offered by any of UCT's six faculties
Demonstrate academic talent and a commitment to excellence
Face significant social and economic barriers to accessing higher education
Demonstrate potential for transformative and ethical leadership
Be committed to serving communities and contributing to positive change
Only applicants who receive an offer of admission to UCT will be eligible for the programme
requirements: Submit an application for academic study and placement to the University of Cape Town first; the scholarship application will not be considered otherwise
Hold a UCT campus ID or applicant number, needed to submit the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application
Complete the separate Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application form with all required uploads
Applications are considered even if a firm UCT admission offer has not yet been received
documents: UCT campus ID or applicant number, full name exactly as on the birth certificate or passport, and the email address used to apply to UCT
Proof of address, e.g. an official bank statement, a utility bill, a council or municipal services bill, or a letter from school to parents or caregiver
Financial status documents, e.g. parents' or guardian's bank statements or details of social or government grants the family receives
Number of people living in the household
Curriculum Vitae or Resume of no more than 3 pages covering educational background, employment history, extracurricular activities, community engagement and leadership positions

Essay of no more than 2,000 words (postgraduate: leadership qualities and how the programme will empower contribution to economic growth and social development, including community service or leadership/entrepreneurship initiatives)
One letter of recommendation from a school teacher or lecturer, pastor or other religious leader, or previous employer, including the referee's full name and contact details
Disclosure of any applications to other Mastercard Foundation Scholars Programs at partner universities
All supporting documentation must be presented in the English language
selection_criteria: Academically talented with a demonstrated commitment to learning and a drive to complete your education
Limited in the ability to access education owing to significant financial barriers
Committed to investing in the community through the skills and knowledge acquired
A future leader committed to ethical transformation and making a positive contribution to the community and broader society
coverage: Tuition fees for the chosen programme of study
Annual travel to and from UCT
application_method: STEP 1 - Review UCT's study options at https://uct.ac.za/applicants-and-students
STEP 2 - Submit the application to the University of Cape Town at applyonline.uct.ac.za
STEP 3 - Submit the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application via the programme application form using the UCT campus ID or applicant number
official.application_route: Two separate applications: apply to UCT for admission first, then complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application form with the UCT campus ID/applicant number; only applicants who receive an offer of admission to UCT are eligible for the award.
official.study_mode: Full-time; the programme does not cover part-time studies
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of an African country, including South Africa; UCT encourages applications from refugees and forcibly displaced youth
official.international_eligibility: No for non-African nationals - the award is restricted to citizens of African countries, including South Africa
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any field offered by UCT's six faculties: Commerce, Engineering & the Built Environment, Health Sciences, Humanities, Law or Science. Not covered: part-time studies or qualifications by research only (Master's by dissertation or PhD). Students admitted to the Integrated Master's Programme through the African Climate & Development Initiative or Healthy Futures South Africa via the Africa Health Collaborative are also eligible.
official.duration: Covers the full period of the student's UCT programme of study; renewable annually subject to satisfactory academic performance and personal conduct and participation in the programme's development activities
official.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cape Town, delivered in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, provides scholarships and comprehensive support to academically talented young people who face significant social and economic barriers to accessing higher education. UCT frames it as more than a scholarship: an opportunity to unlock potential, grow as an ethical leader and join a lifelong network of changemakers. It covers the full period of the student's UCT programme of study for a first bachelor's degree or an eligible taught postgraduate qualification.
official.region: Africa (catalogue region); UCT states the programme selects academically talented young leaders from Sub-Saharan Africa
official.program_type: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program - a foundation-funded scholarship with comprehensive academic, psychosocial and financial support, administered by the University of Cape Town in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation

verification.notes: Verified against UCT's own programme overview, apply, how-apply, application-form and FAQ pages: coverage, eligibility, deadlines and required documents are published, but UCT states no rand value for the award and no IELTS/TOEFL requirement for the scholarship itself.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-cost award: UCT covers tuition, campus accommodation, living expenses, medical aid, a laptop, a study visa where needed and annual travel, so cost should not force you to drop out. The trap is sequencing - you must apply to UCT for admission first, obtain your campus ID or applicant number, and only then submit the separate scholarship form, because only admitted students can receive the award. Postgraduate applications for the 2027 intake close 31 October 2026, so plan for both submissions inside the same window. Since UCT publishes no rand figure, budget against the actual fee and residence costs of your chosen programme rather than a headline amount.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African citizens facing significant financial barriers who want a full-cost first bachelor's, honours, postgraduate diploma or coursework master's place at UCT and can evidence community service and ethical leadership.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply to UCT for admission first and safeguard the campus ID or applicant number - the scholarship form cannot be submitted without it
Gather proof of address and financial-status documents (parents' or guardians' bank statements, or records of social or government grants) before opening the form
Draft the 2,000-word essay as a leadership-and-impact narrative with concrete community service examples rather than a generic personal statement
Secure a recommendation letter from a teacher, lecturer, religious leader or previous employer, including their full contact details
Keep the CV to three pages covering education, work, extracurriculars, community engagement and leadership positions
Confirm your faculty's programme-specific closing date, since faculty deadlines can fall before the scholarship deadline
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the scholarship application without first applying to UCT - UCT states such applications will not be considered
Thin evidence of financial need: the form exists to identify candidates facing significant barriers, so weak financial-status uploads can sink a strong academic profile
Targeting an excluded qualification: part-time study and research-only degrees (Master's by dissertation, PhD) are not covered
An essay that asserts leadership without describing actual initiatives or community service
Missing an earlier faculty admission deadline so the UCT application never reaches the stage the scholarship requires
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: UCT publishes no rand value for the award, so budget from UCT's published tuition and residence rates. Costs outside the published cover - personal spending beyond living-expense support, dependants' expenses and travel beyond the annual allowance - would be self-funded.
document_audit: Every upload field must be completed: the form states you must upload each type of required document for the application to be considered
Files are capped at 40 MB each and restricted to formats such as pdf, doc/docx, rtf, txt and odt - check scans before uploading
The name entered must match the birth certificate or passport exactly
The recommendation letter must carry the referee's full name and contact details
The form asks whether you applied to other Mastercard Foundation Scholars Programs; answer it accurately, as UCT allocates awards fairly across the network
alerts: Undergraduate applications for the 2027 intake closed on 30 September 2026; only postgraduate applications remain open until 31 October 2026
A UCT admission offer is a hard eligibility condition - no offer, no scholarship, even with a completed funding application
Some UCT faculties run earlier programme-specific deadlines than the 31 October scholarship deadline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Two-stage: submit the UCT admission application online first, then use the resulting campus ID or applicant number to complete the separate scholarship form with all uploads before the deadline.
